## Proof

**Setup.** Each cell of the $n\times n$ grid takes a value in $\{1,\dots,n\}$. For each row and each column, either all entries are equal ("flat") or all entries are distinct ("sharp"). Since a line has $n$ cells with values in $\{1,\dots,n\}$, "sharp" means a permutation of $\{1,\dots,n\}$.

**Key structural lemma.** Let $F_R, S_R$ be the flat/sharp rows and $F_C, S_C$ the flat/sharp columns.

- If two flat rows share a value $v$ and some column is sharp, that column would contain $v$ twice — impossible. So if $S_C\neq\varnothing$, all flat-row values are distinct.
- Dually, if $S_R\neq\varnothing$, all flat-column values are distinct.
- A flat row of value $v$ and a flat column of value $w$ meet at a cell forced to be both $v$ and $w$, so $v=w$.

**Case A: all rows flat ($S_R=\varnothing$).** Every column equals the same vector $(r_1,\dots,r_n)$, so it is valid iff this vector is constant or a permutation. Constant $r_i=v$: $S=n^2 v$, giving $\{n^2,2n^2,\dots,n^3\}$. Permutation: $S=n^2(n+1)/2$.

**Case B: all columns flat.** Symmetric, same values.

**Case C: both $S_R,S_C\neq\varnothing$ (mixed).** From the lemma: at most one flat row and at most one flat column, and if both exist they share the same value $v$.

- (i) 0 flat rows, 0 flat cols (Latin square): every column sums to $n(n+1)/2$, so $S=n^2(n+1)/2$.
- (ii) 1 flat row (value $v$), 0 flat cols: all columns sharp, each sums to $n(n+1)/2$, so $S=n^2(n+1)/2$.
- (iii) 0 flat rows, 1 flat col: all rows sharp, each sums to $n(n+1)/2$, so $S=n^2(n+1)/2$.
- (iv) 1 flat row (value $v$), 1 flat col (value $v$): the flat column contributes $n v$; the other $n-1$ sharp columns each sum to $n(n+1)/2$. The $(n{-}1)\times(n{-}1)$ subgrid is a Latin square on $\{1,\dots,n\}\setminus\{v\}$ (exists for $n\ge 2$), so
$$S = nv + (n-1)\cdot\frac{n(n+1)}{2} = nv + \frac{n(n^2-1)}{2}, \quad v=1,\dots,n.$$

**Collecting all values.** The attainable sums are exactly
$$P=\{kn^2:1\le k\le n\},\quad Q=\Big\{\tfrac{n^2(n+1)}{2}\Big\},\quad R=\Big\{nv+\tfrac{n(n^2-1)}{2}:1\le v\le n\Big\}.$$

**Overlaps.** $Q\in P \iff (n+1)/2\in\mathbb Z\iff n$ odd; $Q\in R\iff v=(n+1)/2$ integer $\iff n$ odd. For $P\cap R$: $kn^2=nv+\tfrac{n(n^2-1)/2}$ gives $v=kn-\tfrac{n^2-1}{2}$, integer only when $n$ is odd, and one checks the unique solution in range is $k=v=(n+1)/2$, yielding the single common value $Q$. So:
- $n$ **even**: $P,Q,R$ pairwise disjoint, $|P|=n, |Q|=1, |R|=n$ $\Rightarrow$ $V(n)=2n+1$.
- $n$ **odd**: the three sets meet only at the single point $Q$, so $V(n)=n+1+n-1=2n-1$.

Equivalently $V(n)=2n+(-1)^n$.

**Summation.**
$$\sum_{n=1}^{10}V(n)=\sum_{n=1}^{10}\bigl(2n+(-1)^n\bigr)=2\cdot\frac{10\cdot 11}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{10}(-1)^n=110+0=110.$$

**Verification of small cases.** $V(1)=1$, $V(2)=5$ (sums $\{4,5,6,7,8\}$), $V(3)=5$ (sums $\{9,15,18,21,27\}$), $V(4)=9$, $V(5)=9$, $V(6)=13$, $V(7)=13$, $V(8)=17$, $V(9)=17$, $V(10)=21$. Total $=1+5+5+9+9+13+13+17+17+21=110$.

$$\boxed{110}$$

## Proof

**Setup.** Each cell of the $n\times n$ grid takes a value in $\{1,\dots,n\}$. For each row and each column, either all entries are equal ("flat") or all entries are distinct ("sharp"). Since a line has $n$ cells with values in $\{1,\dots,n\}$, "sharp" means a permutation of $\{1,\dots,n\}$.

**Key structural lemma.** Let $F_R, S_R$ be the flat/sharp rows and $F_C, S_C$ the flat/sharp columns.

- If two flat rows share a value $v$ and some column is sharp, that column would contain $v$ twice — impossible. So if $S_C\neq\varnothing$, all flat-row values are distinct.
- Dually, if $S_R\neq\varnothing$, all flat-column values are distinct.
- A flat row of value $v$ and a flat column of value $w$ meet at a cell forced to be both $v$ and $w$, so $v=w$.

**Case A: all rows flat ($S_R=\varnothing$).** Every column equals the same vector $(r_1,\dots,r_n)$, so it is valid iff this vector is constant or a permutation. Constant $r_i=v$: $S=n^2 v$, giving $\{n^2,2n^2,\dots,n^3\}$. Permutation: $S=n^2(n+1)/2$.

**Case B: all columns flat.** Symmetric, same values.

**Case C: both $S_R,S_C\neq\varnothing$ (mixed).** From the lemma: at most one flat row and at most one flat column, and if both exist they share the same value $v$.

- (i) 0 flat rows, 0 flat cols (Latin square): every column sums to $n(n+1)/2$, so $S=n^2(n+1)/2$.
- (ii) 1 flat row (value $v$), 0 flat cols: all columns sharp, each sums to $n(n+1)/2$, so $S=n^2(n+1)/2$.
- (iii) 0 flat rows, 1 flat col: all rows sharp, each sums to $n(n+1)/2$, so $S=n^2(n+1)/2$.
- (iv) 1 flat row (value $v$), 1 flat col (value $v$): the flat column contributes $n v$; the other $n-1$ sharp columns each sum to $n(n+1)/2$. The $(n{-}1)\times(n{-}1)$ subgrid is a Latin square on $\{1,\dots,n\}\setminus\{v\}$ (exists for $n\ge 2$), so
$$S = nv + (n-1)\cdot\frac{n(n+1)}{2} = nv + \frac{n(n^2-1)}{2}, \quad v=1,\dots,n.$$

**Collecting all values.** The attainable sums are exactly
$$P=\{kn^2:1\le k\le n\},\quad Q=\Big\{\tfrac{n^2(n+1)}{2}\Big\},\quad R=\Big\{nv+\tfrac{n(n^2-1)}{2}:1\le v\le n\Big\}.$$

**Overlaps.** $Q\in P \iff (n+1)/2\in\mathbb Z\iff n$ odd; $Q\in R\iff v=(n+1)/2$ integer $\iff n$ odd. For $P\cap R$: $kn^2=nv+\tfrac{n(n^2-1)/2}$ gives $v=kn-\tfrac{n^2-1}{2}$, integer only when $n$ is odd, and one checks the unique solution in range is $k=v=(n+1)/2$, yielding the single common value $Q$. So:
- $n$ **even**: $P,Q,R$ pairwise disjoint, $|P|=n, |Q|=1, |R|=n$ $\Rightarrow$ $V(n)=2n+1$.
- $n$ **odd**: the three sets meet only at the single point $Q$, so $V(n)=n+1+n-1=2n-1$.

Equivalently $V(n)=2n+(-1)^n$.

**Summation.**
$$\sum_{n=1}^{10}V(n)=\sum_{n=1}^{10}\bigl(2n+(-1)^n\bigr)=2\cdot\frac{10\cdot 11}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{10}(-1)^n=110+0=110.$$

**Verification of small cases.** $V(1)=1$, $V(2)=5$ (sums $\{4,5,6,7,8\}$), $V(3)=5$ (sums $\{9,15,18,21,27\}$), $V(4)=9$, $V(5)=9$, $V(6)=13$, $V(7)=13$, $V(8)=17$, $V(9)=17$, $V(10)=21$. Total $=1+5+5+9+9+13+13+17+17+21=110$.

$$\boxed{110}$$
